text:
sara: Customer (Acme infra) reports structured output failing when they enable strict JSON enforcement. They get an HTML error page and their parser bombs. Repro attached below.

maya: Can you paste the exact curl they used?

sara: Here it is (redacted API key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"open-variant","prompt":"...","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```

sara: Customer also included Accept header implicitly from their client (was defaulting to text/html). They say we return 500 with HTML body.

devlin: Do we see the response headers from our side? If Accept is text/html some frameworks will fallback to an HTML error page.

sara: Captured response from our gateway: 
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 1243

<html>...stack trace...</html>
```

devlin: Hmm. I can reproduce locally: POST with response_format=json & strict=true but Accept: text/html leads to the error-page path rather than our JSON-enforcement path. Looks like a header-negotiation regression after the routing change last week.

maya: Customer is blocked (parsing fails downstream). Any short term workaround we can tell them?

devlin: Workaround: force Accept to application/json or explicitly include response_format=structured_object (client-side). Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Accept: application/json\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"open-variant","prompt":"...","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```
This should force our code path to return JSON (or a 422 structured error) rather than HTML.

devlin: I'll open an internal issue and push a hotfix to ensure response_format and strict mode win over Accept fallback. Escalating to eng-runtime: INFR-1423.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary at 2028-05-14T18:00Z (rollout INFR-1423).

sara: Told customer the workaround and gave an ETA for canary. Customer confirmed workaround works for now.

devlin: Pushed fix to canary, monitoring for 30m. Confirmed TTL: canary returned JSON for the repro.

sara: Customer verified receipt of JSON and parser now succeeds. Closing for now, will keep INFR-1423 open until prod rollout. :thumbsup:
